title: Slicing a smooth morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a
smooth morphism of schemes. Then
there exists an etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ such that
$U_i\to S$ factors as $U_i\to V_i\to S$ where $V_i\to S$ is etale and
$U_i\to V_i$ is a smooth morphism of affine schemes, which has a
section, and has geometrically
connected fibres.
(*Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, [Tag `0EY4`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY4) = Lemma
37.38.8.*)

proof.text: Use the existing Lean pointwise slicing argument: dense separable fibre points give an etale slice; its pullback has a section. Apply lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-geometrically-irreducible to its relative component. Take an affine open around a preimage of the desired point, pass to its open image, and slice a second time to obtain affine source and base with a section and geometrically connected fibres. Shrink to affine neighbourhoods first to meet the quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses. Assemble the pointwise factorizations by choice into the covering indexed by the points of X. These arguments are already proved in this module; the new relative-component proof supplies its last missing ingredient.
